PR objectui#11972 (draft, 1 commit `5f049697` on the base `a835c3149` — the merge base, confirmed with `git merge-base`; the commit carries the model-free `Claude-Session` / `Co-authored-by` trailer pair; 9 files, +322/−7; head repository = base repository, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, assignee `huangyiirene`, no auto-merge, `mergeable_state` clean, `Part of #11070 (round 13)` as its first line with no closing keyword), round 13 of card objectui#11070: the three class (ii) pairs round 12's M3 re-run left, on the seat's answers A, B and C in the ACCEPT `6060086777` — claim `6060489789`, dev report `6061531921` (`status: done`, `open_questions: []`). Inputs: the card body and its 70 comments; the PR body, its file list and the net diff against `main` at this head (`main` has since taken 3 commits over 37 files — `7546570a4`, `0c9fb8ea3` and `d7e9e9ab6`, the last being objectui#6152 round 8 on `objectql.ts` / `objectql.zod.ts` and the view plugins — with 0 files in common with this PR's 9, so the head's check-runs are not stale for them); and the 43 check-runs on the head: 40 success, 3 skipped by design (`dependabot`, the two coverage shards), 0 failure — `Type Check`, `Lint`, the eight `Test` shards and the `Test` roll-up, `Test (dist pins)`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Doc Fence Language Check`, `Doc Example Id Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Build Docs`, `Build & E2E`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `Docs Route Eager Closure Check`, the five `Changeset` gates, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Pre-Install Import Graph Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Bundle Analysis`, `README Export Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Action Ref Convention`, `Shell Escape Residue Scan`, `Skill Example Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Skill Eval Token Check` and `label` among them. The gate verdicts are those conclusions; nothing was built, run or re-run here. Where a judgment below needed a fact the diff's context lines do not carry, the head tree was read with `git show` / `git grep` at `5f049697` — `packages/i18n/src/currency.ts`, `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, `packages/fields/src/widgets/{NumberField,PercentField,FormulaField,SummaryField,CurrencyField}.tsx`, `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx`, `packages/types/src/field-types.ts`, `content/docs/fields/currency.mdx`, `content/docs/blocks/*.mdx`, the pin's helpers and the `form-field-zod-coverage` assertions — each named at its use; that is a read of the PR's own tree, not a run. No `@objectstack/spec` copy is present in the shared checkout, so every statement about the spec's `FieldSchema` below rests on the pins the `Test` shards ran green, named where it does. No earlier `## Contract review` names this head: the PR thread carries one bot comment (the console performance budget) and 0 reviews, and the card's newest record (`5934528537`) names PR #11387's `cbc637c2`.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface move the diff implies, each judged:

- **The strict face WIDENS on `form` · `fields[]` by two keys: `scale` and `currencyConfig`.** `FormFieldSchema` (zod) gains `scale: stripImportedDefaults(SpecFieldSchema).shape.scale` and `currencyConfig: stripImportedDefaults(SpecFieldSchema).shape.currencyConfig` — the spec's own `FieldSchema` members by reference, the pattern rounds 2 through 10 used for `multiple`, `rows`, `accept`, `dimensions`, `reference`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength` and `columns` on this same face (`form.zod.ts:1098-1106` at the head). RIGHT — the declare route of the triage direction (`5888862869`: declare on both faces when authors write it and a renderer reads it), and exactly answers A and B's declared home in the ACCEPT. The writers are the five catalog documents (`fields-number/with-decimal-places`, `fields-percent/required-percent`, `fields-percent/with-decimal-places` for `scale`; the two `fields-currency` documents for `currencyConfig` after this diff). The readers are in-code and named: `NumberField.tsx:41` (`numberField?.scale`, the step), `PercentField.tsx:126` (`resolveFieldScale({ type: 'percent', scale: percentField?.scale })`), `FormulaField.tsx:95` and `SummaryField.tsx:61` through `formatNumberFieldValue` (whose `number-format.ts` imports `resolveFieldScale`), and `CurrencyField` through `resolveFieldCurrency` (`packages/i18n/src/currency.ts:46`, limb 2: `config?.currencyMode === 'fixed' ? config.defaultCurrency : undefined`). Not a `.passthrough()` flip and not an exemption list — `strict-authoring-face.ts` is absent from the file list; the keys are shape members. Pinned where it can fail: the two `FIELD_CASES` rows (each parses on the strict face and a misspelled sibling is refused by name), `form-field-zod-coverage`'s exact key-set equality (`Object.keys(FormFieldSchema.shape)` equals `DECLARED_KEYS` plus the refused-by-name keys, read at the head), and the new catalog pin that parses all five documents on `StrictAnyComponentSchema`; the dev's A1 / A2 ablations (each zod member deleted through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven) turned 11 and 9 red as predicted, taken as reported. True width: this face is flat, so both keys are accepted on every `fields[]` entry whatever its `type` — as every key rounds 1 through 12 declared here — named so the widening is read at its real width.
- **The tolerant face NARROWS on the same two keys: a malformed value is refused where the base stripped the key unjudged.** A `scale` that is not a whole number from 0 to 100 (2.5, −1, 101, the string `'2'`), a `currencyMode` outside `fixed` / `dynamic`, a `defaultCurrency` that is not three characters, and the removed `currencyConfig.precision` are now refused on `AnyComponentSchema` as on the strict face. RIGHT — the arithmetic consequence of declaring the spec's members on a face that used to strip them, the same shape rounds 1, 3, 7, 10, 11 and 12 priced; seven `WRONG` rows pin it on both faces, and the values-kept row pins that `scale: 1` and a fixed `currencyConfig` survive the tolerant parse while `currencyConfig: {}` stays `{}` — the imported-defaults boundary keeping the spec's `dynamic` / `CNY` out of the document, which `resolveFieldCurrency`'s own docblock (read at the head) says must not render as yuan. Stated in the changeset under BREAKING with the fix. The dev's M3 says no corpus document writes either malformed shape and "red today" moves only by the guide's fence; taken as reported.
- **Both faces refuse `scale` on a `type: 'currency'` entry, `custom` at `scale`, with the spec's text — one spec cross-key rule carried locally.** The `superRefine` arm adds `ctx.addIssue({ code: 'custom', path: ['scale'], message: CURRENCY_FIELD_SCALE_REFUSAL })` when `field.type === 'currency' && field.scale !== undefined`. RIGHT, and the one judgment in this diff that is a design rather than a reference: a member taken off `.shape` carries none of the spec's cross-key rules, so a bare declaration would have made the strict face newly ACCEPT exactly the document the spec refuses (at the base it was refused as an undeclared key) and that nothing reads — `CurrencyField.tsx:28-34` says in its own comment that it reads neither `precision` nor `scale`, because objectstack#19629 ruling B took `scale` off the `currency` type. So nothing is refused that the spec admits (the pin's first assertion is that `SpecFieldSchema` itself refuses `{ type: 'currency', scale: 2 }` with `custom` at `scale`), and the only text restated from the spec is guarded by an equality pin against the spec's issue message, which is the right cue: a spec release that drops or rewords the rule reds the pin before the copy drifts. On the strict face this is a refusal that changes code (`unrecognized_keys` to `custom`), not an accept-set move; on the tolerant face it is a narrowing, stated. Keyed on `type` as the spec keys it, so an entry drawn as currency through `widget` alone with another `type` is not judged — the PR body states that width. The asymmetry — this rule carried, the spec's `rows` / `minLength` / `maxLength` / `multiple` rules not — is reasoned in the diff's own docblock and holds: those key on the spec's field-type sets, and this face's `type` is a widget id the spec's `FieldSchema` refuses outright (the dev measured `type: 'input'` refused at `type`), so carrying them would refuse what this face's own `input` branch honours; the existing by-reference members have never carried them. The dev's A3 ablation (the rule disarmed) turned exactly the one predicted row red.
- **The TypeScript face: `FormField.scale?: SpecField['scale']` and `FormField.currencyConfig?: SpecField['currencyConfig']`, by reference.** RIGHT. `SpecField` is `Field` from `@objectstack/spec/data` (`form.ts:23`), the same import the face's other by-reference members use. Both keys used to fall to `FormField`'s `[key: string]: any` index signature (present at the head, `form.ts:1906`), so a literal with a string `scale` or an unknown `currencyMode` is now a compile error, exactly as the changeset says. Pinned by `assertionScaleAndCurrencyConfigBySpecReference` — an `IsAny` row and two exact `Equal` rows — in the `Type Check` program; the dev's A4 ablation (the TS `scale` member deleted) turned the predicted `tsc` errors and no vitest row. The docblock's "a typed literal cannot refuse it, because this interface keeps an index signature" is true at the head.
- **The two currency catalog documents move from `currency` to `currencyConfig { currencyMode: 'fixed', defaultCurrency }`; `currency` stays undeclared.** RIGHT — answer B verbatim; the spec's declared home, which `resolveFieldCurrency` limb 2 honours (read at the head). The strict face still refuses `fields[].currency` by name (pinned), and no other corpus document writes `currency` as a field key (`git grep` over `examples` and `content` at the head: 0 JSON hits) — H1 held. Rendering pinned through the real `SchemaRenderer`, form renderer and `@object-ui/fields` registration: `€` / `$` with step `0.01`, a `dynamic` control drawing no symbol, a `JPY` control drawing `¥` with step `1` — so the declaration, not a constant, decides both; the `Test` shards ran it green. The ACCEPT's unstated premise — that objectui's face already accepted `currencyConfig` — fell, and the dev declared it rather than trade `form · fields[].currency` for `form · fields[].currencyConfig` (still class (ii), since `resolveFieldCurrency` reads it); judged under ③.
- **The guide's `action:button` fence names its endpoint `target`; the sentence below it is rewritten.** RIGHT — answer C verbatim. Face: pinned, the taught node parses on both faces and `endpoint` in the bag stays refused on both. Runtime, read at the head: `ActionRunner.ts:1143` maps `api` in `builtinExecutors` to `executeAPI`, which resolves `action.api || action.endpoint || action.target` (`:2269`), and `action-button.tsx:293` forwards `schema.target` — so a typed `actionType: 'api'` with `target` alone executes, and `action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx:288` already mounts exactly that shape (`actionType: 'api', target: '/api/probe', method: 'PUT'`). Each clause of the new sentence holds: "an `api` action's endpoint is its `target`, with the verb in `method`" (the runner's `method = action.method || 'POST'`), "the spec's `action:button` row refuses `endpoint` and names `target`" (the pin's refusal, and `layout.md:684` already teaches the same), and the unchanged half "`api` is not a key any action renderer forwards" (the renderer's forward list at the head is `target`, `endpoint`, `bodyExtra`, `bodyShape`, `locations`, `enabled`, `size` — no `api`). The three `content/docs/blocks/*.mdx` fences that still write `endpoint` (`authentication.mdx:63`, `ecommerce.mdx:60`, `forms.mdx:102`) are `button` nodes carrying `action: { type: 'submit', endpoint, method }` — round 12's class (i) pair `button · action`, not an `action:button` properties key — so leaving them is right.
- **Exclusions held.** `objectql.ts` / `zod/objectql.zod.ts` untouched (objectui#6152 round 8's, and `d7e9e9ab6` on `main` now carries them with no overlap here); `resolveFieldCurrency` untouched (`packages/i18n` absent from the list); `ActionRunner` untouched; no `strict-authoring-face.ts`; no `package.json`; no governed path among the 9 (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). Beyond the claim's named files: the new catalog pin and the `form-field-zod-coverage` key list — both tests, inside "with their tests"; and the `currencyConfig` declaration, inside the claim's two named files but beyond its stated purpose, judged under ③.
- **Head = the reviewed head.** One commit, no merge, no force-push; the net diff's 9 files and +322/−7 equal the PR's; every check-run ran on it.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes` agrees across the claim (`6060489789`), the PR body's second line ("yes — widens: … narrows: …", both effects named) and the changeset ("**Clause-②: yes (widening)**"). Judged against what the diff publishes: the strict accept set of a published export (`StrictAnyComponentSchema`'s `form` `fields[]`) widens by two keys — the primary direction, the move the round was dispatched for — and the tolerant face narrows on the same keys' malformed values plus the currency rule, both halves stated with the fix. RIGHT; the round-10, -11 and -12 reading of this mixed shape. The claim's closing sentence ("B and C correct documents and widen nothing") is the one line the diff outgrows: B widens by `currencyConfig`, and the PR body's own `Clause-②` line and the changeset state it; `yes` was already the level, so the level does not move — see ③.
- `.changeset/11070-form-field-scale-currency-config.md`: `@object-ui/types` **minor**.
